title: FII inflows spark re-rating, lift Nifty Bank to record high - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Among the stocks that scaled fresh all-time high included ICICI Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Punjab National Bank, Karnataka Bank, Karur Vysya Bank, Dhanlaxmi Bank and Union Bank of India

Banking stocks rallied sharply, pushing the Nifty Bank index to an all-time high of 62,273.5, as foreign investors turned optimistic on the sector after a prolonged period of underperformance.

Of the 14 stocks in the index, 12 rallied with Punjab National Bank leading the pack. The public sector bank rallied 3.74 per cent to ₹150 a piece, IDFC First Bank and AU Bank increased 2.8 per cent and 2.2 per cent, respectively.

Among the stocks that scaled fresh all-time high included ICICI Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Punjab National Bank, Karnataka Bank, Karur Vysya Bank, Dhanlaxmi Bank and Union Bank of India.

The inflow is largely attributed to improved FII interest in these stocks. Indian markets have has particularly received good FII inflows in November, momentarily moving away from global AI trend. Financial services sector received a large chunk of this and the banking stocks benefitted from this, say analysts.

“Banks have been underperforming for the last two years despite delivering strong lending growth and healthy earnings. A large part of the weakness came from heavy FII selling, as financials account for 30-40 per cent of foreign investors India exposure,” said Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Financial Services.

The inflows however were not uniform. Bigger banks rallied slower than than the smaller peers. “When that money is coming to India, it’s finding some pockets where valuations are still cheap,” said Siddharth Rajpurohit, Lead Banking analyst at Systematix Group. He further said that ICICI Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank have already had their run.

“The risk-reward is strong in financials. If FII inflows continue, banks, especially private banks, can continue to outperform,” Nair said. He cautioned that near-term profit booking cannot be ruled out after the market’s recent rally, but believes large-cap financials are well placed to benefit from sustained domestic inflows, stronger-than-expected corporate earnings and improving foreign investor sentiment.

According to Kotak Securities, banks delivered a healthy 20 per cent y-o-y earnings growth in Q2-FY27, led by lower provisions, while operating profit growth stood at around 15 per cent.

“A rising rate cycle, a better loan mix and a relatively well-positioned liability franchise should aid further acceleration in NII growth from the current levels. We retain our positive outlook on asset quality and benign credit costs in the near term.,” the domestic brokerage said in a note.
